thread:
support-jamie: Heads-up — Lumenix (dedicated pool dp-431) just reported sustained 429s during a marketing spike. They say burst credits show >0 in dashboard but traffic is being admitted at a lower TPS than before and app SLOs hit. Root seen at ~14:23 UTC. Logs below.

ops-bot: alert: admissions_slo_violation pool=dp-431 account=lumenix-acc-09 429_rate=0.18 observed_tps=210 configured_tps=300 :rotating_light:

rishi-sre: Do we have autoscale events or recent capacity churn for dp-431? Any noisy neighbor alerts?

support-jamie: Customer sent a quick repro: they send parallel streaming requests with small prompts. Example request:

```bash
curl -s -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/dp-431/generate 
  -d '{"model":"open-rtx-q4", "max_tokens":256, "streams":true}'
```

tanya-runtime: Looking at admission logs now. I see admission decisions returning "deny" with reason=admission_credit_depleted even though the credits ledger shows ~120 credits at 14:20. However the admission accounting shows credits_consumed spike from long-lived streaming sessions. Also seeing two pods with sustained GPU-util 98% (possible noisy neighbors) which reduces available headroom.

kevin-ml: Model variant changed last week to quantized-v2; token-per-request profile shifted a bit — more backend tokens per call when using streaming. Could explain faster burn. But shouldn't cause mismatch between ledger and admission accounting.

support-jamie: Pasting relevant snippet from admission-controller logs (scrubbed):

```
[2025-10-03T14:21:12Z] pool=dp-431 acct=lumenix-acc-09 req_id=abc123 admit=false reason=admission_credit_depleted credits_seen=120 credits_accounted=0 credits_consumed=34 window=60s
[2025-10-03T14:21:45Z] pool=dp-431 acct=lumenix-acc-09 req_id=abc456 admit=false reason=noisy_neighbor_penalty noisy_pod=pod-gtk-21 gpu_util=99%
```

tanya-runtime: That first line looks like a race in the credits reconciliation path — ledger updated but the in-memory counter used by admission isn't getting refreshed fast enough under churn. I can hotfix to force-sync ledger on credit-check for the next 30s while we investigate. Also will mark the two noisy pods for throttling.

marco-accounts: Contract notes: Lumenix has a guaranteed headroom SLA of 20% during campaign windows (per sales order). If we throttle their requests due to noisy neighbors that's a breach. We need to prioritize correction and offer credits if any downtime.

amanda-billing: I'm seeing a reconciliation lag on the credits ledger: event stream processing falling behind (~90s lag) for account lumenix-acc-09 around the incident window. Opening billing ticket to re-run reconciliation for that range and attach event IDs.

rishi-sre: Immediate mitigation plan (short checklist):
1) Force-sync credits on admission path for lumenix-acc-09 (tanya)
2) Throttle/isolated noisy pods in dp-431 (tanya)
3) Increase admission headroom for lumenix by +10% temporarily (ops)
4) Run targeted autoscale pre-warm for next 15m (ops)
5) Billing reconciliation and customer credit review (amanda, marco)

support-jamie: I told the customer we have a patch ETA ~25m and gave backstop guidance: client retry with exponential backoff + respect Retry-After header. They acknowledged and asked for root cause and whether dedicated headroom config was changed.

tanya-runtime: Implemented hotfix on canary: admission now does an immediate ledger sync for accounts with >5 concurrent streams. Can confirmed in dp-431-canary — 10k requests replayed, 429s dropped from 12% -> 0.6%. Rolling patch to dp-431 now. Commands used: `kubectl -n infra exec -it adm-ctrl -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/refresh-ledger?acct=lumenix-acc-09` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/admission-controller -n dp-431` (canary -> prod roll within 3m).

rishi-sre: Also applied a temporary admission headroom bump: lumenix headroom from 20% -> 30% for 60m and pinned a pre-warm policy: target_prewarm_tps = max(estimated_tps*1.5, 350). Added throttling rule: noisy pods with gpu_util>95% get 50% request rate until drain.

amanda-billing: Reconciliation job queued; I will post event IDs and any refund recommendations once run completes. Will propose one month of surplus credits if ledger shows we deducted during the lag window.

marco-accounts: I informed the account owner and scheduled an update call. We'll cover SLA impact and next steps (pre-warm runbook + campaign headroom planning).

support-jamie: Customer confirmed reduction in 429s and appreciates the fast roll. I'll keep thread open until billing + account owner confirm. Action items: postmortem, update headroom docs, add credits-sync metric to SLO dashboard. @tanya-runtime @amanda-billing @marco-accounts please follow. :thumbsup:

tanya-runtime: Filed internal PR with tests for credits-refresh path and added e2e that simulates concurrent streaming burn. PR #4621. Will link after merge.

rishi-sre: Postmortem checklist created and assigned. Follow-up deliverables: (a) fix race in in-memory credits cache (b) autoscaler prewarm tuning guide (c) billing reconciliation alerting.

support-jamie: Closing customer loop after billing confirms. Will paste final notes and add to support KB under "dedicated: burst credit reconciliation & pre-warm playbook".
